title: What SQLAlchemy Does
content:
******1. Database Abstraction**
**SQLAlchemy allows you to write Python code to interact **with various SQL databases (like PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, etc.) without writing raw SQL queries.


**2. ORM (Object Relational Mapper)**
You can **define your database tables as Python classes**. These classes can then be used to insert, update, delete, or query data—just like working with normal Python objects.




** Why Use SQLAlchemy? **
✅ Cross-database compatibility

✅ Avoids repetitive boilerplate SQL

✅ ORM makes it easier to work with complex relationships

✅ Secure and prevents SQL injection

✅ Large community and documentation

title: Be Careful using Session
content:
• If you don’t commit, the changes won’t be saved to the database.

• If you reuse sessions too broadly, like globally across threads or requests (in a web app), it can cause bugs.

**Best Practice**
• Use session per unit of work.

• Always close or remove the session after you're done using it:



[code-snippet-0

OR

[code-snippet-1]
This automatically handles closing the session.
codeSnippets:
session.commit()
session.close()
with Session() as session:
    # operations
    session.commit()

title: what will happen if we do not close the session
content:
• If you don’t close a SQLAlchemy session, here’s what can happen

**⚠️ 1. Memory Leaks**
The session holds references to all objects you’ve loaded or modified. If you don’t close it, these references stay in memory and can pile up—leading to memory leaks and increased RAM usage.

**⚠️ 2. Database Connection Not Released**
Each session keeps a connection to the database. If you don’t close the session:

The connection may remain open, reducing the number of connections available in the pool.

Over time, this may exhaust your database connections, especially in high-load environments like web apps or APIs.

**⚠️ 3. Uncommitted Changes**
If you don’t commit and close, any pending changes will be lost if the app crashes or restarts, and the transaction might stay open, causing database locks.

**⚠️ 4. Thread Safety Issues**
In multi-threaded apps (like Flask, FastAPI), reusing or not closing sessions can result in:

Cross-thread access issues

Data inconsistency

Weird bugs that are hard to trace


**✅ Best Practice**
Use with context manager or try-finally pattern:




[code-snippet-0]
OR

[code-snippet-1]

 **Built-in Exception Handling**

• If an error occurs in the block:

• The session is rolled back automatically if you use Session.begin()

• It still closes the session (whether error or success)

Example with transaction management:

[code-snippet-2]
codeSnippets:
# Safe usage with context manager (SQLAlchemy 1.4+)
with Session() as session:
    # Do DB operations
    session.commit()
# Session auto-closes here
# Manual safe pattern
session = Session()
try:
    # DB operations
    session.commit()
finally:
    session.close()
with Session.begin() as session:
    session.add(user1)
    session.add(user2)
# If any add fails, the whole transaction rolls back automatically

title: How to cretae a Modal in SQLAlchemy
codeSnippets:
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
Base = declarative_base()


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'users'  # table name in the DB

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String(50), nullable=False)
    email = Column(String(100), unique=True)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User(id={self.id}, name='{self.name}', email='{self.email}')>"

title: Types of ViewSet and when we use what?
content:
In Django REST Framework (DRF), **ViewSets **are used to simplify the creation of views for **RESTful APIs**. Instead of writing individual methods for** handling HTTP verbs like GET, POST, etc., you define a ViewSet and DRF handles routing automatically** (especially when using routers).


[code-snippet-0]


**1. ViewSet **
^• Use When: You want full control over each action (list, create, retrieve, etc.)

^• You Write: All logic yourself.

^• Example Use Case: Custom business logic for each HTTP method.
[code-snippet-1]


**2. GenericViewSet **
^• Use When: You want flexibility with built-in mixins (ListModelMixin, CreateModelMixin, etc.)

^• You Compose: Only the functionality you need.

^• Example Use Case: Only list and create support, no update/delete.
[code-snippet-2]


**3. ReadOnlyModelViewSet**
^• Use When: API is read-only (e.g., public product catalog, FAQs)

^• Provides: list() and retrieve() methods

^• No Create/Update/Delete
[code-snippet-3]


**4. ModelViewSet**
^• Use When: You need full CRUD operations

^• Provides: All actions (list, retrieve, create, update, partial_update, destroy)

^• Quick and Powerful

[code-snippet-4]


**Summary Decision Guide**
[code-snippet-5]
codeSnippets:
| Type                   | Base Class                                     | Purpose                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ViewSet`              | `rest_framework.viewsets.ViewSet`              | Manual control over all methods (`list`, `retrieve`, `create`, etc.) |
| `GenericViewSet`       | `rest_framework.viewsets.GenericViewSet`       | Combine with mixins for flexibility                                  |
| `ReadOnlyModelViewSet` | `rest_framework.viewsets.ReadOnlyModelViewSet` | Only allows `GET` (`list` and `retrieve`)                            |
| `ModelViewSet`         | `rest_framework.viewsets.ModelViewSet`         | Full CRUD support out of the box                                     |
class CustomViewSet(ViewSet):
    def list(self, request):
        ^# Custom list logic
        pass

    def create(self, request):
        ^# Custom create logic
        pass
from rest_framework.mixins import ListModelMixin, CreateModelMixin

class ListCreateViewSet(ListModelMixin, CreateModelMixin, GenericViewSet):
    queryset = Post.objects.all()
    serializer_class = PostSerializer
class PostReadOnlyViewSet(ReadOnlyModelViewSet):
    queryset = Post.objects.all()
    serializer_class = PostSerializer
class PostViewSet(ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Post.objects.all()
    serializer_class = PostSerializer
| Scenario                 | Recommended ViewSet          |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| Custom logic needed      | `ViewSet`                    |
| Only some methods needed | `GenericViewSet` with mixins |
| Read-only API            | `ReadOnlyModelViewSet`       |
| Full CRUD API            | `ModelViewSet`               |
